title: Source-etale locality, without derived descent
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $u:U\to X$ be a surjective etale morphism of separated
finite-type schemes. If $fu:U\to Y$ is cohomologically smooth, then
$f:X\to Y$ is cohomologically smooth. Every etale map $u$ is
cohomologically smooth, with $\omega_u\simeq\Lambda$.

proof.text: Use the finite purity setting and its canonical Nagata compactifications and invertible coefficient exponent. Work in the existing compared predicate: its tensor and base-change arrows are literally comparison images of the ordinary-etale canonical maps. The source library already proves the ordinary-etale locality argument in WeilConjectures.EtaleCohomology.Purity.Smooth.CohomologicallySmooth, so reuse its component results rather than reproving the compact-support mate identities.

proof.text: The exact faithful comparison pullback reflects isomorphisms: homology commutes with the exact functor, and the sheaf comparison reflects isomorphisms. Full faithfulness of comparison with bounded-below target lifts an isomorphism whose target is the coefficient unit. Given a pro-etale Dctf inverse of nu* W, take its etale-origin witness and use tensor and unit comparison to lift both inverse isomorphisms. Thus compared invertibility implies ordinary-etale invertibility.

proof.text: The source-library results isInvertible_dualizingComplex_of_comp and isIso_dualizingComplexTensorMap_of_comp descend the first two ordinary-etale clauses along the surjective etale cover, using its invertible dualizing object and its dimension-zero canonical tensor isomorphisms. For the compared inverse construct N = RHom(omega_f, unit) explicitly. Exceptional finite-Tor preservation places omega_f in Dctf, and finiteCoefficient_derivedHom_ctf_etale places N in Dctf over the algebraically closed field. In a closed symmetric monoidal category an invertible W has RHom(W, unit) as its tensor inverse: exactPairingOfTensorIso and ihomObjUnitIso give the two product isomorphisms. Comparison preserves Dctf, tensor and the unit, so nu* N is the required compared inverse. Applying comparison to the descended tensor map proves the second clause. The tensor-map composition criterion uses exists_rightDerivedLowerShriekCompIso, owned by lem-route-exists-right-derived-lower-shriek-comp-iso, and projectionMapAssociativity, owned by lem-route-projection-map-associativity. Exceptional preservation is invoked through the native pro-etale constructibleFiniteTor_rightDerivedUpperShriek interface of lem-sf-native-finite-tor-preservation. Its value on nu* unit is identified with nu* omega_f by rightDerivedUpperShriekComparisonIso. Full faithfulness lifts its bounded constructible origin and exact tensor comparison reflects its Tor interval. For Hom use the actual Sheaf declaration finiteCoefficient_derivedHom_ctf_etale of thm-sf-hom-ctf, after the explicit equivalence of the two etale constructibility and Tor predicates. The complete compiled-data audit reaches eight sorry leaves: AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.exists_rightDerivedLowerShriekCompIso (owned by lem-route-exists-right-derived-lower-shriek-comp-iso); AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.exists_smooth_compact_dual_model (owned by lem-asd-smooth-compact-dual-model); AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.sfEtaleCompactProjectionInverse_composition (owned by lem-sf-etale-compact-projection-coherence); AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.sfEtaleGraphExchangeTensor (owned by lem-sf-etale-graph-exchange-tensor); AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.sfEtaleGraphTransferTensor (owned by lem-sf-etale-graph-transfer-tensor); AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.sfAffineBaseP1TraceAdjunction (owned by lem-sf-affine-base-p1-trace-adjunction); AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.projectiveLineExceptionalBaseChange (owned by lem-asd-projective-line-exceptional-base-change); AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.nonempty_normalizedProjectiveLineAdjunction (owned by lem-normalized-projective-line-adjunction). No other sorry leaf occurs in the two proof terms and their types.

proof.text: For each allowed finite-type Cartesian square of f, pull back the source cover. Give its source the composed structure map to the field; it remains finite type and the pasted square is therefore in the domain of the assumed compared base-change clause. Reflect that clause through comparison. The existing ordinary-etale etaleBaseChange and isIso_rightDerivedUpperShriekBaseChangeMap_comp_iff identify invertibility for the pasted square with invertibility of exceptional pullback of the f base-change map. The surjective-etale conservativity theorem isIso_of_isIso_rightDerivedUpperShriek_map reflects the latter. Convert between the dualizing and exceptional unit maps and apply comparison. No absolute separatedness is imposed on the new schemes. Its compact-support composition and exchange coherence input is exists_rightDerivedLowerShriekCompIso, cited with its own route node. Etale base change uses the normalized compactificationEtaleAdjunction and its unit compatibility, via etaleBaseChange; it does not use smooth exceptional base change or affine-line purity.

source.place: Locality argument, implemented step 4; source-library canonical-map APIs named in the text

proof.text: For the etale assertion, isIso_compactificationEtaleComparison gives the normalized etale compactification adjunction. Right-adjoint uniqueness identifies the existing exceptional functor with ordinary pullback, and its value on the unit is the unit by leftDerivedUpperStarUnitIso. Applying comparison and its unit isomorphism gives the stated untwisted dualizing isomorphism. The pro-etale unit is Dctf, and the unitors give both tensor-inverse isomorphisms. The existing ordinary-etale dimension-zero tensor theorem and the normalized etaleBaseChange adjunction argument give exactly the canonical tensor and base-change maps; comparison transports them to the remaining clauses. Empty schemes require no separate choice or nonemptiness hypothesis. In particular the base-change clause is obtained from etaleBaseChange and isIso_dualizingComplexBaseChangeMap_iff, avoiding isCohomologicallySmooth_of_etale and its smooth-purity dependency.
